title: AI Creators: Build Real Things with AI
tagline: A year-long, hands-on course where students learn HOW to use AI tools and WHY they work. They leave with a portfolio of pictures, videos, a website, an AI helper, an app and a game. Every lesson works 1-on-1 or with a group, in easy-to-read words.
audience: College students (18+) · any AI experience · 1-on-1 or small group · easy, 4th-grade reading level
budget: Free tools first. Gemini on a school Google account is the main tool. Up to about $20 a month for ONE teacher account used for demos.

progression.studentsCan: Explain in plain words how AI guesses from patterns, write a prompt with the recipe, and follow the Safety Pact.
Make single pictures and videos on purpose (camera, style, hooks, timing) and always add an AI label.
Put pieces together into one product: a web page with clear parts, a path for visitors and a call to action.
Build helpers that do steps for you: a starting signal, actions, tools and a human check.
Plan and build an app with AI help: screens, buttons, saved info and login. Test it and fix bugs.
Design games with rules, a fun loop and feedback. Test with players, make it better, and show it off.

lessonTemplate.purpose: Quick recall of last lesson's ideas, plus a hook. Gets brains on before screens open.
One big idea with a picture and a worked example. Short, so it doesn't overload memory.
The student makes something real, with a checklist. 1-on-1, you sit beside them and ask questions instead of giving answers.
A fun challenge that uses the idea. Group: houses compete. 1-on-1: student vs. Team Bolt (you).
Group: gallery walk and feedback. 1-on-1: the student teaches it back to you, and you trade feedback.
2 or 3 quick questions. 1-on-1, ask them out loud. Use the answers to plan the next lesson.

safetyThreads.how: Students use every tool on their own accounts. Before using one, check what it does with your info and your work, and turn off AI training where you can.
Never put real photos, videos or voices of other people into AI without their clear 'yes'. Use yourself, objects, free public pictures, or AI-made characters.
No real brand logos, famous people or copied characters. Make your own brands. Say where things came from.
Label AI-made work (#MadeWithAI). Ads must be honest: no fake reviews or fake buyers.
Never share full names, school, address, passwords or secret codes with AI or online. Use nicknames.
AI can be sure and wrong (hallucination). Every module has a 'Spot the AI mistake' activity.
